Q: How to correctly manage date and timezone between frontend and database A:

Your instinct is correct. The "just store UTC" advice is for apps that only care about instants in time, which is most of them and why it's become "standard" advice. Yours cares about what the wall-clock time.

Something like this gives you both:

procedure_at  TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,  -- UTC, for ordering and comparisons
timezone      TEXT NOT NULL           -- "Australia/Sydney"

UTC gives you a universal timeline for sorting and cross-timezone comparisons if you ever need it and the IANA timezone name lets you convert back to the correct wall clock time for that specific date. The tz database should have historical rules so it applies the offset that was in effect at the time, not today's offset.

To report "all procedures on the 12th," convert procedure_at to the stored timezone and filter on the local date.

Your DateTimeOffset approach will work too because you get the wall clock time directly and can derive UTC from the offset. You just lose the named location, so +11:00 could be Sydney or Solomon Islands. For a medical app where the location context probably matters, I'd go with the IANA name. I think most platforms have good support for it at this point.

Q: Fetching Git behind proxy in Docker container A:

Thanks to @VonC for pointing me in the right direction

Here is the solution to fix the problem for Github

git config --global url."https://github.com/".insteadOf git@github.com:
git config --global url."https://".insteadOf git://

For bit bucket:

git config --global url."https://user:pass@bitbucket.org".insteadOf   ssh://git@bitbucket.org
